title: Deploy lifecycle state machine with a self-loop and a late 'rolled back' state
persona: Dana, a platform engineer on the internal deploy tool 'shipit', sketches the lifecycle of one deploy before asking an agent to add a 'cancelled' state, because the status badges in the UI and the database disagree.
topic: the states a shipit deploy goes through
realism: Lifecycle state machines are drawn constantly when someone is about to add a state: ovals, a diamond for the one real decision, a loop on the state that retries, and the moment of 'wait, that's not where it goes' when a terminal state turns out to be two different things. The colours are the badge colours in the UI, so she uses them without thinking and then says what they mean.

steps.say: This is the lifecycle of one deploy in shipit, the way I picture it.
Then a runner picks it up and it's building.
Building includes the tests, and then there's really one decision, are the tests green.
If yes it goes to deploying.
And waiting is called queued, that's what the badge in the UI says, I should use the same word.
Deploying loops on itself, it hits the health check and retries, up to five times I think, or maybe it's time based, not sure.
And if the health checks never pass, it's failed.
Green is where you want to end up, red is the bad ending, same as the badges.
Hmm, wait, that's not right, a failed health check doesn't just fail.
It rolls back automatically to the previous release. Failed is only when the build or the tests break.
So I'm moving failed over and adding rolled back, that's the missing one, from deploying.
Orange means it ended and nothing is broken in prod, it just didn't ship.

steps.note: is 'cancelled' a real state today, or just failed with a reason?

steps.say: I think you can re-run a failed one, but I don't know if that makes a new deploy or sends the same one back to queued.
That's the part I'd want checked against the code.

story: the states in order are queued -> building -> (tests green?) -> deploying -> live; the diamond is the one decision: tests green, yes goes to deploying, no goes to failed
deploying has a self-loop: it retries the health check, up to 5 times she thinks, or it may be time based
the first state was called 'waiting' and she renamed it 'queued' to match the UI badge
she first drew deploying -> failed on health check failure, then deleted it: a failing health check rolls back automatically to the previous release, and 'failed' only means the build or tests broke
'rolled back' is the state she realised was missing and added late, reached from deploying after 5 failed checks
colours match the UI badges: green (live) is the good ending, red (failed) the bad ending, orange (rolled back) means it ended without breaking prod but didn't ship
'failed' was moved left only to make room for 'rolled back'
she circled 'failed' because she does not know whether re-running a failed deploy creates a new deploy or sends the same one back to queued
she wants to know whether 'cancelled' exists today or is just failed with a reason (the change she is about to make)
partner_should_ask_about: whether re-running a failed deploy is a new record or a transition failed -> queued (the circled, unsure part)
whether the health-check self-loop is bounded by count (5) or by time
what happens to a deploy that is rolled back: can it be retried, and is the previous release then 'live' again?
where a cancel could happen today (from queued, building, deploying?), given she typed she doesn't know if cancelled exists
